hypothesis: The density-weight multiplicative update band `[LOWER_PCOF, UPPER_PCOF]` and its HPWL-ratio exponent control how fast density pressure ramps; widening the lower bound so the weight can also *decrease* when HPWL worsens (currently it is clamped to a narrow band that mostly grows) will let the placer spend more iterations on wirelength/timing before density dominates, giving rsz more slack headroom on moderately-critical nets (TNS).
expected_effect: WNS slightly better or neutral, TNS improves (fewer moderate violations), overflow unchanged (still <=300), runtime unchanged.
analysis: The hypothesis held: all three cases improved, with dTNS gains of +10.0%, +30.5%, and +15.7% and dWNS gains of +5.9%, +15.3%, and +9.0%, consistent with the proposed mechanism—allowing the density weight to decrease when HPWL worsens lets the placer prioritize wirelength/timing longer, giving rsz more slack headroom on critical nets. Overflow (~116–140) stayed moderate, so gains aren't from density collapse. Next step: sweep the widened lower bound (e.g., 0.5×, 0.25× current LOWER_PCOF) and the HPWL-ratio exponent across seeds to confirm robustness and find the best trade-off before adopting.
